body:
PR #2830 round 2 is pushed. Head: 4802c26f4f17ea2d37b1396ccb33a6a9d2a8fa1e (two commits on top of your 0225e2b8b3).

1. [blocker] Portability: the bwrap test's sh helper is gated with an item-level linux cfg. check-portability.sh passes. This was also the red gates job.
2. role enter refuses before minting when stdout is a terminal, and names `eval "$(aida role enter <seat>)"`. Related: the secret is now minted only where a session keyring exists, so macOS and Windows stay process-bound with no adopt-key line. task_1597_delegation_prompt broke on the new refusal (it ran a bare role enter on a PTY); it now captures stdout to a file on Unix, as eval does.
3. Docs and the --bg refusal no longer suggest --bind-pid for bg seats.
4. Revoke removes the grant lock and sweeps the locks of revoked, expired or vanished grants. Tested.
5. xtrace state is saved and restored around adopt-key.
6. lib-1: the only failure was the resolver ratchet (aida-05's FYI). The eval text now uses resolve_aida_exe. No stray/ failure appeared in that run, so I dropped that note.

RESIDUAL, for you to rule on: if xtrace is already on in the interactive shell, bash traces the `eval "<text>"` invocation itself, secret included, before any line of the text runs. The C3 guard only stops tracing of the commands inside. I verified this in bash. Closing it needs the secret to reach adopt-key by a path other than the eval text. That is a design change, so it is not in this round. It is written up in the PR body.

C4 operator probe: the exact steps and an evidence template are in the PR body.

Gates:
- targeted tests: 53/53 lib, task_1597 1/1, bwrap 3/3
- check-portability: 0
- make check-ci-fast: 34 gates green
- make test-touched: exit 0

Nothing was shipped, merged or self-approved.
